findings.title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results via zip
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, the code does `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id whose iteration order follows the backend's query order, not the order of `error_ids`, and any missing node is simply absent from the dict. If any one error event is missing from nodestore (expired/deleted), every subsequent pairing shifts by one, so each ErrorEvent gets the wrong `id` attached to the wrong event's title/message, and the final error_ids entries are silently dropped. The result is error context injected into the Seer summary prompt with incorrect event IDs and missing errors. The lookup should map back by node id instead of relying on positional zip, e.g. iterate `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and read `events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget path renders hardcoded empty table, discarding real query results
findings.body: In WidgetCardChart.tableResultComponent, when the organization has the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the actual `tableResults`/`result.data`/`result.meta` that were just fetched. If this flag is ever enabled for an organization, every table widget on their dashboards will render a permanently empty table (columns is an empty array, so no headers or rows render at all), and the loading/error/fieldAlias handling in the existing SimpleTableChart path is bypassed entirely. This is clearly a placeholder that should not be merged as-is; either wire the real `result.data`/`result.meta`/fields into TableWidgetVisualization or don't branch on the flag yet.

findings.title: Assemble analytics event recorded before feature-flag and schema validation
findings.body: The new `analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...)` call is placed at the top of `post`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check (which returns 404) and before `validate_preprod_artifact_schema` (which returns 400). As a result the analytics event fires for requests from orgs without the feature and for malformed requests, inflating the metric with failed/no-op calls and making it unusable as a measure of actual assemble usage. Move the record call below the feature check and schema validation (or after the task is successfully enqueued).

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validation uses truthiness, so age=0 bypasses it
findings.body: BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` to enforce that the two fields are mutually exclusive. Because `age` is an IntegerField, a report containing `"age": 0` together with a `timestamp` passes both validators (0 is falsy), accepting a report that mixes the two spec formats the serializer is explicitly designed to reject. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None` instead of truthiness.

findings.title: Falsy check on custom cell renderer causes valid falsy renders to be discarded
findings.body: In renderDefaultBodyCell (and the same pattern in renderDefaultHeadCell at line 32), the custom renderer result is checked with `if (cell) { return cell; }` before falling back to the default renderer. The documented contract is that returning `undefined` opts into the fallback, but a custom renderer that legitimately returns `0`, `""`, or `null` (e.g. a cell that intentionally renders an empty value) will be silently replaced by the default field renderer's output, producing incorrect cell content. Check `cell !== undefined` instead so only an explicit undefined triggers the fallback.
